items.title: Plotters, kingmakers and dark horses — the Liberals vying for control
items.description: Parliament House has entered the spill zone, where politics is at its most primal. Here are the Liberals jostling for control of their much-reduced party.

items.title: Live: Senior Liberal says party at 'change or die' moment ahead of vote on leadership tomorrow
items.description: Angus Taylor has confirmed he will challenge Opposition Leader Sussan Ley for the leadership at the meeting. Follow live.

items.title: RBA governor accused by senator of 'gaslighting' Australians on economy
items.description: Reserve Bank governor Michele Bullock fires back at Nationals senator Matt Canavan after he accused her of "gaslighting" Australians over the state of the Australian economy.

items.title: Muslim leader urges public apology over police 'manhandling'
items.description: The Lebanese Muslim Association's secretary says the community's relationship with police could be fractured following the Sydney protest despite spending "nearly 20 years repairing" the damage caused by the Cronulla Riot.

items.title: 'This is over for me, I'm done': Woman says man assaulted her on solo bush hike
items.description: A woman's solo hike through regional Victoria took a disturbing turn near Daylesford, raising questions about safety and police responses.

items.title: Multiple people rescued in Alice Springs flooding, one still stranded
items.description: Northern Territory emergency services are still working to reach one person isolated by flooding in Alice Springs, after rescuing multiple people earlier this morning.

items.title: PM condemns 'white supremacy ideology' behind alleged Invasion Day terror attack
items.description: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has condemned the "racism and hatred" and "white supremacy ideology" behind the alleged terrorist attack on the Invasion Day rally in Borloo/Perth last month.

items.title: Protesters, police gather as Herzog's Melbourne visit gets underway
items.description: Isaac Herzog has begun addressing Jewish leaders and dignitaries at an event in Southbank, while demonstrators protest the Israeli president's visit outside.

items.title: Former CFMEU official among three arrested in anti-corruption probe
items.description: The arrests were made hours before Premier Jacinta Allan faced reporters over separate allegations detailed in a new report that $15 billion in taxpayer dollars had made its way into the hands of criminals who had infiltrated the union.

items.title: Epstein files hearing descends into shouting matches
items.description: US Attorney-General Pam Bondi faces furious questions over the censorship of names in the Epstein files at a heated hearing before a committee of Congress.

items.title: 'Large crack' found in $786 million bridge days before opening
items.description: Days before the official opening, the Tasmanian government's largest-ever infrastructure project hit a hurdle, with a large crack picked up in one of the Bridgewater Bridge's piers detected and fixed, documents show.

items.title: What young people think of One Nation's rising popularity
items.description: Recent opinion polls have found that, for the first time, One Nation is the second-most popular party with voters, overtaking the Coalition. So what do teenagers think of One Nation and do they still trust the major parties?

items.title: Man missing in Tasmanian bushland for four days found alive
items.description: The 32-year-old man went into a bushland with a friend to collect firewood on Sunday. Police say he has been found alive at the bottom of a steep incline.

items.title: James Van Der Beek will always be Dawson Leery. He embraced it with humour
items.description: James Van Der Beek's death has prompted wide-ranging tributes from co-stars and friends who praised his kindness and humour.

items.title: The abandoned base that's left a toxic legacy in Antarctica
items.description: The ABC has been given rare access to an abandoned Australian base in Antarctica that continues to pose a threat to the environment.

items.title: UK police vow speedy decision over Andrew-Epstein trade documents
items.description: British police say they are "making progress as quickly as possible" on whether to launch a full investigation into allegations that Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor shared confidential trade documents with late financier and sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

items.title: Baker Boy on racism, mud crab and reshaping his positive persona
items.description: The Yolŋu artist known as the Fresh Prince of Arnhem Land is the king of feel-good bilingual bangers. But heavy is the crown.

items.title: $10m worth of cannabis plants allegedly seized on NSW property
items.description: Police allege the four people charged were cultivating a large-scale cannabis farm in the Riverina.

items.title: Live: ANZ shares hit record high on cost-cutting program
items.description: Australian stocks are trading higher, with major companies, including ANZ, Origin Energy, AMP and Temple & Webster, releasing earnings results today. Follow the latest updates in our live blog.

items.title: SA Labor releases audio of Liberal MP backtracking on key policy at private event
items.description: South Australia's Treasurer says the Liberal Party has secretly dumped its major $495 million policy less than six weeks out from the state election, with the Opposition arguing it has to wind back Labor's tax due to state budget blowouts.

items.title: Children as young as 10 on bail to be fitted with ankle bracelets in Queensland
items.description: Magistrates will now be able to order children as young as 10 to wear electronic monitoring devices as a bail condition.

items.title: Chris Minns positions himself as the anti-protest premier. Will it pay off?
items.description: By expanding police powers and allowing bans on authorised public assemblies the Minns government has made restricting protest a defining feature of its first term.

items.title: Ex-police officer jailed for arson and possession of bestiality videos
items.description: A former NSW police officer is jailed for multiple offences, including arson and possession of bestiality videos, while stationed at a rural border post.

items.title: Israel's demolition of a soccer pitch in the West Bank sparks international campaign
items.description: A campaign to save a West Bank football pitch from demolition has gone global. The sport's most powerful bodies, as well as social media influencers, have intervened to pressure Israeli authorities to reconsider its destruction.

items.title: Feral camels searching for water descend on remote communities
items.description: Large mobs of camels are wreaking havoc in remote Indigenous communities as they desperately search for water.
